subject: Hospitality
title: André Balazs: Hotels as Theaters
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: André Balazs: Hotels as Theaters.

hook.text: André Balazs sees hotels not as buildings but as theaters—every space is a stage, every moment a performance.

buildup.text: His properties—Chateau Marmont, The Standard, Chiltern Firehouse—are famous for scene-making more than room counts.

discovery.text: Balazs designs lobbies as social theaters where seeing and being seen is the product. The lobby is the show.

twist.text: Chateau Marmont is deliberately never renovated to perfection. Its faded glamour is the aesthetic—imperfection as luxury.

climax.text: Balazs proved that hotels can be cultural institutions, not just places to sleep. His properties shape city social scenes.

punchline.text: Not accommodation but theater. Balazs made hotels cultural stages.

quiz.question: What is André Balazs' approach to hotel design?
options: Hotels as theaters—every space is a stage for social performance
